text:
clara: quick brain dump from arch sync 1: can we make the scheduler decide "spill to cold lane" based on request "shape entropy" + explicit profile header? idea: router tags requests with X-Batch-Profile (low_entropy | high_entropy | interactive) and scheduler maps entropy->window_ms probabilistically. keeps router cheap and gives scheduler a single scalar to reason with.

josh: how do we compute entropy cheaply in router? worried about CPU on the hot path.

clara: don't run full n-gram or model. use two heuristics: token_count_variance (last-k tokens) and punctuation_density. cheap bit ops and counters, O(1) per request. thresholding yields entropy_buckets.

priya: we should gate which clients can set X-Batch-Profile. otherwise noisy clients will mark everything interactive. auth + server-side override sounds right.

dan: fairness note 1: heavy high_entropy batches could hog aggregator. propose token-weighted admission credits per tenant: each tenant gets N tokens/sec budget; scheduler consumes credits when admitting batch. credits refill token-wise so small interactive requests don't starve.

josh: token-weighted sounds good. add softbackoff: if tenant exhausted, route new requests to cold lane (higher latency but safe) then throttle. explicit fallback helps SLA.

priya: telemetry wishlist: per-profile admitted_rate, per-profile p99 latency, token_utilization, mislabel_rate (header vs heuristic), and per-tenant credit_balance. need dashboards before canary.

clara: experiment plan: incremental canary across stages: 
1) Only emit X-Batch-Profile header from router (no scheduler change) for 24h, collect mislabel_rate + distribution.
2) Enable scheduler mapping: profile->window_ms mapping with conservative values (windows +2x of baseline) for 48h.
3) Gradually widen mapping based on 48h results.

dan: also add a fast rollback: if p99 for interactive profile crosses threshold or mislabel_rate > 5%, immediately revert mapping. tie to rollout system.

josh: small config snippet suggestion:
```
router:
  profile_header: X-Batch-Profile
  heuristic:
    token_variance_k: 8
    punct_density_thresh: 0.12
  auth_only_override: true

scheduler:
  profile_map:
    interactive: { window_ms: 4, max_tokens: 128 }
    low_entropy: { window_ms: 16, max_tokens: 1024 }
    high_entropy: { window_ms: 32, max_tokens: 2048 }
  tenant_credits:
    refill_tokens_per_sec: 5000
    soft_fallback: cold_lane
```

priya: we need to consider model sensitivity to batching prefixes. add per-model min_samples_for_batching and an eval hook sampling 1 in 500 requests for output drift if window_ms changes. connect that to alerts.

clara: good call. also, power-of-two windows for metrics buckets would be nice. dan, can we make credit accounting approximate to reduce lock contention? e.g., local token reservoirs per thread with periodic sync.

dan: yes, approximate leaky-bucket reservoirs per worker thread and periodic reconciliation is doable. we should simulate contention with synthetic tenants first.

josh: A/B idea: compare three policies in lab: baseline fixed-window, profile-based scheduler, profile-based + token-credits. measure p50/p90/p99, cost_per_token, batch_fill_rate, and cross-tenant fairness (tail ratio).

runtime-bot: canary plan created: routers/profile-proxy v1.2 -> canary stage started :rocket: (canary_id=cp-2026-03-21)

priya: action items: (1) clara + josh: prototype router heuristic + header emit (2) dan: implement approximate token reservoirs + cold_lane fallback (3) priya: dashboards + eval hooks (4) devex: doc header and auth policy. set a 2-week experiment window.

clara: thanks all 1: Ill open a short RFC with config examples and a small sim dataset. posting sim results next week.
